verdicts.claim: SQLite automatically triggers a checkpoint after 1000 WAL pages
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'By default, SQLite does a checkpoint automatically when the WAL file reaches a threshold size of 1000 pages.'
Neither cited page states a byte size; WebSearch found no primary source for 4 MiB. It is derived arithmetic that holds only for 4096-byte pages.

verdicts.claim: unless overridden by PRAGMA wal_autocheckpoint or sqlite3_wal_autocheckpoint()
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: threshold 'can be changed or ... disabled using the wal_autocheckpoint pragma or by calling the sqlite3_wal_autocheckpoint() C interface.'

verdicts.claim: Manual checkpointing via sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2 and PRAGMA wal_checkpoint, supporting modes PASSIVE (no writer blocking)
verdicts.evidence: c3ref: PASSIVE checkpoints 'without waiting for any database readers or writers to finish'; pragma.html lists PASSIVE/FULL/RESTART/TRUNCATE.
c3ref: 'This mode blocks new database writers while it is pending, but new database readers are allowed to continue unimpeded.'
c3ref: RESTART blocks new writers and 'ensures that the next writer will restart the log file from the beginning' (paraphrased loosely as 'resets WAL header').

verdicts.claim: TRUNCATE (blocks and truncates the WAL file after checkpoint)
verdicts.evidence: c3ref: TRUNCATE 'works the same way as SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_RESTART with the addition that it also truncates the log file to zero bytes just prior to a successful return.'

verdicts.claim: The WAL-Reset race bug, which could silently lose data when a checkpoint raced with a writer
verdicts.evidence: Tailscale: a write during a checkpoint can leave pages uncopied so 'that data is permanently lost'; a write 'vanished into thin air without raising an error.'

verdicts.claim: existed through SQLite 3.51.2 and was fixed in SQLite 3.51.3 (released March 2026)
verdicts.evidence: Tailscale confirms 3.51.3 'only contained a fix for the WAL-Reset bug' but gives no date or affected range; the range and date come from wal.html §11 ([^c1-1], not cited on this bullet): 'present ... from 3.7.0 (2010-07-21) through 3.51.2 (2026-01-09). It is fixed in version 3.51.3 (2026-03-13)'.

verdicts.claim: Long-running readers can starve checkpoints, causing WAL file growth; increasing the frequency of automatic checkpoints via PRAGMA wal_autocheckpoint mitigates
verdicts.evidence: Starvation half supported, but wal.html says auto checkpoints are PASSIVE and 'if ... there is always at least one active reader, then no checkpoints will be able to complete and hence the WAL file will grow without bound'; its mitigation is 'reader gaps' or manual RESTART/TRUNCATE, not more frequent autocheckpoints. Tailscale does not discuss reader starvation.
